newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia PM satisfied with deputy on sale.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia PM satisfied with deputy on sale.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard said on Wednesday he was broadly satisfied with Trade Minister Tim Fischer's decision to sell his shares.
"I was broadly satisfied with what he had to say," Howard told reporters.
Fischer said he had chosen to sell his shares not because the ministerial guidelines required him to but because he wanted to be extra cautious in avoiding conflicts of interest.

Fischer denied in a radio interview that he had breached Howard's ministerial guidelines, under which government members are required to dispose of any investments which may conflict with their portfolio area.
"I have fully complied with the ministerial guidelines," Fischer earlier told Sydney radio 2UE.
Earlier on Wednesday Howard said it was absurd to suggest that Fischer was wrong to have held resource shares after he became trade minister in March.
The Australian Financial Review newspaper report on Wednesday said Fischer's holdings had included shares in Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd, Clyde Industries Ltd, WMC Ltd, Qantas Airways Ltd and TNT Ltd.
The report said Fischer had sold off shares in major mining and exporting companies over the last few months.
He had also sold some shares since the start of the share row last week, the newspaper reported.
Howard said on Tuesday that the guidelines might have to be changed to allow ministers to use blind trusts, which would prevent them knowing what investments they held.
